scope: All 107 sentence-verified third-person-plural verb forms missing final t in live v019 Latin sources, all in papers 1-43.
choice: Add the required final t to each exact audited third-person-plural form while preserving its stem, aspect, orthography, capitalization, clause, and mathematical meaning.
motivation: Official verb morphology requires third-person-plural -ut/-et and contracted -ajut. Every changed site has an overt plural subject or antecedent, whereas five separately guarded -aju forms are genuine singular authorial predicates. The repair closes a systemic agreement defect without lexical normalization or sentence recasting.
alternatives_rejected: Treat final t as optional: this conflicts with the official third-person-plural paradigm and the edition's earlier accepted repairs.
Rewrite every token ending in -aju: that would corrupt genuine first-person-singular authorial verbs and nouns such as slučaju and algebraju.
Normalize stems at the same time: this would conflate an exact morphology repair with separate lexical and orthographic decisions.

official_verb_grammar.relevance: The third-person-plural endings are -ut/-et; contracted third-conjugation forms end in -ajut.

context_review.finding: All 107 mapped sentences were reviewed and have plural subjects, plural relative antecedents, or coordinated plural predicates.
